function: DDPG allocates transmit power, sensing power and sensing dwell time of UAV aerial base stations in ISAC, maximizing minimum communication rate via radar-assisted beam alignment (p. 8).
system: 4 UAV aerial base stations with radar, 20 ground users, 3 macro base stations; mmWave/THz band, 4 MHz bandwidth; antenna counts not stated; no RIS (pp. 1, 8-9).
method: Deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) reinforcement learning, centralized training and execution at one ABS; fully connected actor and critic, 300-200-100 neurons, replay buffer; replaces SCA (pp. 8-9).
data_channel: Own simulation: free-space path loss and misalignment fading from [4], [30]; GUs from a Poisson cluster process; MBS failure probability 0.5; no dataset or measurement (pp. 4, 9).
test_conditions: One simulated setup (4 ABSs, 20 GUs, 3 MBSs, 50 s cycle); results swept over GUs, ABSs, transmit and sensing power; no train/test shift stated (pp. 9-11).
baselines: Non-learned: SCA optimization, even (AVE) and random (RAND) allocation, BTCT codebook beam training [7]; learned: ML-assisted beam alignment MLA [42] (pp. 9-11).
metrics: Minimum communication rate (Mbps), misalignment error (m), loss value, execution latency (pp. 9-11).
complexity: SCA O((KIJ)^(9/2)) vs DRL O(6(I+G)J x (I+G)J x rho Phi) (p. 8); execution time 0.054-0.132 s (DRL) vs 5.72-15.83 s (SCA) for 12-20 GUs (p. 11).
q1_support: p. 4: "between ABS Aj and GU Ui can be given by [4] and [30]". Free-space path loss (Eq. 2) and misalignment fading come from other papers: custom simulator, no 3GPP model, public ray-tracing dataset or measured data is named.
q2_support: p. 8: "of input layer is (I + G) J and the dimension of output layer". The network size depends on the numbers of GUs, MBSs and ABSs; the sweeps over GUs and ABSs (Figs. 7-8) are not stated as tests of a model trained in another setting.
q3_support: p. 9: "MLA: In [42], the authors propose an machine learning" beam alignment method (learned); non-learned SCA, AVE, RAND and BTCT [7]. p. 11: "the performance of MLA and BTCT are worse than ISAC." Fig. 10 plots DRL against all of them.
q4_support: p. 8: "The computation complexity of DRL-based method" is given as O(6(I+G)J x (I+G)J x rho Phi), against O((KIJ)^(9/2)) for SCA; Table II (p. 11) reports execution latency of DRL and SCA.
q5_support: p. 8: "We deploy J = 4 ABSs, I = 20 GUs, and". The scenario is the paper's own simulation (GU Poisson cluster process, p. 9); no code or data link, public dataset or measurement is mentioned.
notes: ISAC (area 5) and NTN (area 6) both fit; area 6 chosen by the specificity order because the learned DDPG controls transmit and sensing power of UAV aerial base stations (p. 8). SCA is the main solution and DRL replaces it. The only learned baseline is MLA [42], a learned beam alignment method; reviewer may judge whether it counts as the same function for q3. Carrier frequency and antenna numbers are not stated.
